docs.title: Welcome to the AD4x4 API
docs.text: This documentation provides a comprehensive overview of the AD4x4 API, covering everything you need to know to get started. The API is designed to be easy to use and follows standard REST conventions.

docs.title: Main Resources
docs.text:
The AD4x4 API is organized around a few main resources:

  • Authentication and Profiles: Manage user accounts, profiles, and authentication.
  • Trips: Create, manage, and view off-road trips.
  • Meeting Points: Define and manage meeting points for trips.
  • Upgrade Requests: Handle requests for user account upgrades.
  • Account Deletion: Manage the account deletion process.
  • Notifications: Configure and manage user notifications.
  • UI Strings: Retrieve and manage editable UI strings for the client applications.
  • Permissions System: Control user access to different parts of the API.

docs.title: Account Deletion
docs.text: This document explains how a user can request the deletion of their account.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The account deletion process is designed to be simple and secure. It involves two main steps:

  1. The user makes an API request to signal their intent to delete their account.
  2. A background process runs periodically, and after a 3-day grace period, it anonymizes the user's data.

This grace period allows for a "cooling off" period, during which the user can change their mind. The anonymization process ensures that all personally identifiable information is removed from the user's profile, while preserving the integrity of any content they may have created (e.g., trip comments).

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
To initiate the account deletion process, the client must make a POST request to the following endpoint:

POST /api/members/request-deletion

This endpoint does not require any request body. The authenticated user associated with the request will be marked for deletion.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Success

A successful request will return a 200 OK status code and a JSON body indicating success:

{
    "success": true
}

Error: Deletion Request Already Exists

If the user has already requested deletion and a request is pending, the API will return a 400 Bad Request status code and the following JSON error message:

{
    "success": false,
    "message": "deletion_request_already_exists"
}

docs.title: Anonymization Details
docs.text:
After the 3-day grace period, the user's account will be anonymized. This is a permanent and irreversible action. The following fields will be changed:

  • The user will be marked as inactive.
  • The username will be replaced with a randomly generated string (e.g., deleted_user_...).
  • The email address will be changed to a dummy address (e.g., ...@deleted.com).
  • The first name will be set to "Anonymous".
  • The last name will be cleared.

docs.title: Authentication and Profiles
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for user authentication, registration, and profile management.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is handled using JSON Web Tokens (JWT). To access protected endpoints, you must include an Authorization header with a valid JWT access token.

Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>

docs.title: Obtaining a Token
docs.text:
To obtain an access and refresh token pair, make a POST request to the /api/token/ endpoint with the user's credentials.

POST /api/token/

Request Body:

{
    "username": "your_username",
    "password": "your_password"
}

Success Response:

{
    "refresh": "...",
    "access": "..."
}

docs.title: Refreshing a Token
docs.text:
Access tokens are short-lived. When an access token expires, you can obtain a new one by making a POST request to the /api/token/refresh/ endpoint with your refresh token.

POST /api/token/refresh/

Request Body:

{
    "refresh": "your_refresh_token"
}

Success Response:

{
    "access": "..."
}

docs.title: Registration and Password Management
docs.text: The API provides endpoints for user registration and password management, powered by the rest_registration library.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/register/

The request body should include the user's details. Refer to the MemberRegistrationSerializer for the full list of required and optional fields.

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
Authenticated users can change their password by making a POST request to /api/auth/change-password/.

POST /api/auth/change-password/

Request Body:

{
    "old_password": "current_password",
    "password": "new_password",
    "password2": "new_password_confirmation"
}

Note: password and password2 must match.

docs.title: Other Endpoints
docs.text:
The rest_registration library also provides endpoints for: * Resetting a forgotten password * Verifying registration via email

Please refer to the library's documentation for details on these flows.

docs.title: Retrieving a Profile
docs.text:
To retrieve a user's profile, make a GET request to /api/members/{id}/.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Success Response: The response will be a JSON object containing the user's profile information. The fields returned are defined by the ProfileSerializer.

Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., first_name), the API will return camelCase in the response body (e.g., firstName).

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "User",
    "phone": "1234567890",
    "carBrand": "Toyota",
    "carModel": "Land Cruiser",
    "carYear": 2022,
    "carColor": "White",
    "carImage": null,
    "dob": "2000-01-01",
    "iceName": "Jane Doe",
    "icePhone": "0987654321",
    "level": {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Newbie"
    },
    "tripCount": 5,
    "avatar": null,
    "permissions": [...],
    "paidMember": true,
    "dateJoined": "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z",
    "city": "Dubai",
    "gender": "M",
    "nationality": "AE",
    "title": ""
}

docs.title: Updating a Profile
docs.text:
To update a user's profile, make a PATCH request to /api/members/{id}/. Users can only update their own profiles unless they are an administrator.

PATCH /api/members/{id}/

Request Body: The request body should contain the fields to be updated. For a list of editable fields, refer to the EditMemberSerializer. Note that some fields like username, email, and level are read-only.

Success Response: A successful update will return a 200 OK status code and the updated profile data.

docs.title: Editable Strings (UIString) API
docs.text: This document outlines how to use the Editable Strings (UIString) API to manage translations for the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The UIString feature allows for dynamic management of strings in the application's UI. Strings are stored as key-value pairs, with support for English and Arabic translations. The API provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting these strings.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All API endpoints require authentication. You must have the EDIT_UI_STRINGS permission to create, update, or delete UI strings.

docs.title: Retrieve a UI String
docs.text:
• GET /api/strings/{key}/

    Retrieves a single UI string by its key.

    Parameters:

    • key (string): The key of the UI string to retrieve.
    • lang (string, optional): The language to retrieve. Can be en or ar. Defaults to en.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/?lang=ar"

    Example Response:

    json { "key": "welcome_message", "values": { "title": "مرحباً", "body": "مرحباً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }

docs.title: Create a UI String
docs.text:
• POST /api/strings/

    Creates a new UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "new_feature_announcement", "values_en": { "title": "New Feature!", "description": "We have a new feature for you to try." }, "values_ar": { "title": "ميزة جديدة!", "description": "لدينا ميزة جديدة لتجربتها." } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/"

docs.title: Update a UI String
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/strings/{key}/

    Updates an existing UI string.

    Example Request (PUT):

    bash curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "welcome_message", "values_en": { "title": "Welcome", "body": "Welcome to our app!" }, "values_ar": { "title": "أهلاً بك", "body": "أهلاً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

    Example Request (PATCH):

    bash curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "values_en": { "title": "Welcome Back", "body": "Welcome back to our app!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Delete a UI String
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/strings/{key}/

    Deletes a UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
The following validation rules apply when creating or updating UI strings:

  • key: A unique string used to identify the UI string. This field is required when creating a new string and cannot be changed after creation.
  • values_en: A JSON object containing the English translations. This field is required, and its keys define the structure that values_ar must follow.
  • values_ar: A JSON object containing the Arabic translations. This field is optional and can be null or an empty JSON object ({}). If values_ar is provided and is not empty, it must contain the exact same set of keys as values_en.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text: Occasionally, the AD4x4 API may need to be taken offline for maintenance. When this happens, the API will be put into maintenance mode, and all API requests will receive a 503 Service Unavailable response.

docs.title: Client-Side Handling
docs.text:
Client applications should be designed to handle this response gracefully. When a 503 response is received, the client should:

  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that the application is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance.
  • Avoid retrying immediately: Do not immediately retry the request, as this will only add to the server load. Instead, wait a reasonable amount of time before attempting to connect again.

docs.title: Meeting Points
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing meeting points.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Meeting points are predefined locations where trip participants can gather. The API provides endpoints for creating, viewing, updating, and deleting these points.

docs.title: List Meeting Points
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/
    • Retrieves a list of all available meeting points.

docs.title: Retrieve a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single meeting point.

docs.title: Create a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• POST /api/meetingpoints/
    • Creates a new meeting point. Requires the CREATE_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • Request Body: json { "name": "Al Faya", "lat": 24.733, "lon": 55.766, "link": "https://goo.gl/maps/...", "area": "AUH" } Note: The area field can be one of DXB, NOR, AUH, AAN, or LIW.

docs.title: Update a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Updates an existing meeting point. Requires the EDIT_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • The request body should contain the fields to be updated.

docs.title: Delete a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Deletes a meeting point. Requires the DELETE_MEETING_POINTS permission.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: This document outlines the different types of push and email notifications sent by the backend.

docs.title: Registering for Push Notifications
docs.text:
To receive push notifications, the client application must register the device's FCM token with the backend. This is done by making a POST request to the /api/device/fcm/ endpoint.

POST /api/device/fcm/

Request Body:

{
    "registration_id": "your-fcm-token",
    "type": "ios"
}

The type can be ios, android, or web.

For more information on Firebase Cloud Messaging, please refer to the official documentation.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
• New Trip Notification: Sent when a new trip is created.
  • Trip Approval Notification: Sent when a trip is approved or rejected.
  • Accepted from Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are moved from the waitlist to the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Registered List: Sent to a member when they are removed from the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are removed from the waitlist for a trip.
  • New Trip Comment: Sent when a new comment is added to a trip. This is used for the real-time chat feature.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• Upgrade Request Handled: Sent to a member when their upgrade request has been handled (approved or rejected).
  • Upgrade Request Created: Sent to the marshals when a new upgrade request is created.
  • Upgrade Request Reminder: A periodic reminder sent to the marshals about open upgrade requests.

docs.title: Club News
docs.text: • Club-Wide News: Sent to all members when a new club news item is published.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: • Feedback Notification: Sent to the administrators when a member submits feedback.

docs.title: NotificationType Enum Values
docs.text:
The type field in the notification object will contain one of the following enum values:

Value Description NEW_TRIP A new trip has been created. TRIP_APPR A trip has been approved or rejected. WAIT_ACC A user has been accepted from the waitlist. UPG_REQ_HAN An upgrade request has been handled. UPG_REQ_CRE A new upgrade request has been created. UPG_REQ_REM A reminder for an open upgrade request. CLUB_NEWS A new club news item has been published. REM_FROM_TRIP_REG A user has been removed from a trip's registered list. REM_FROM_TRIP_WAIT A user has been removed from a trip's waitlist.

docs.title: Permissions, Groups, and Levels
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the permissions system used in the API. It details the different user groups, experience levels, and the specific actions each group is permitted to perform by default.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
The permissions system is built on three main concepts:

  • Groups: Users are assigned to one or more groups, which determine their general role and permissions.
  • Levels: Levels represent a user's experience or seniority within the club (e.g., Newbie, Intermediate, Marshal). Some permissions are restricted to certain levels.
  • Actions: These are specific permissions that grant the ability to perform a particular operation via the API (e.g., CREATE_TRIP, APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ).

Permissions are granted to groups, and can optionally be restricted to apply only to certain levels.

docs.title: Fetching User Permissions
docs.text:
To get the permissions for a specific user, you can retrieve their profile from the /api/members/{id}/ endpoint. The user's permissions are included in the permissions array in the response.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Example Response Snippet:

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    ...
    "permissions": [
        "CREATE_TRIP",
        "VIEW_CONTACT_INFO"
    ],
    ...
}

docs.title: Groups and Levels
docs.text:
The following table lists the default groups and their corresponding experience levels:

Group Level Numeric Level Notes Newbies Newbie 10 Default for new users Intermediates Intermediate 100 Advanced Advance 200 Experts Expert 300 Disabled by default Explorers Explorer 400 Marshals Marshal 600 Board members Board member 800 Non-level Groups Trip managers N/A N/A Meeting point managers N/A N/A Media managers N/A N/A Upgrade request managers N/A N/A Site admins N/A N/A Super-users with all permissions

docs.title: Default Permissions by Group
docs.text: Here is a breakdown of the default permissions assigned to each group.

docs.title: Explorers
docs.text:
• Can create trips that require approval for the "Newbie" level.
  • Can create trips that do not require approval for "Intermediate" level and above.
  • Can create meeting points.
  • Can view contact information of other members.
  • Can create logbook entries and sign off on skills for trips they lead (Intermediate level and above).

docs.title: Marshals
docs.text:
• Can create trips without requiring approval.
  • Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Board Members
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.
  • Can approve upgrade requests.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.

docs.title: Upgrade Request Managers
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, comment on, edit, and delete upgrade requests.
  • Can delete comments on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Trip Managers
docs.text:
• Can create, edit, approve, and delete trips.
  • Can edit trip registrations and delete trip comments.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.
  • Have superuser permissions for creating logbook entries.

docs.title: Media Managers
docs.text: • Can edit trip media.

docs.title: Meeting Point Managers
docs.text: • Can create, edit, and delete meeting points.

docs.title: Site Admins
docs.text: • Have all permissions.

docs.title: Full List of Permissions (Actions)
docs.text:
The following table lists all possible actions in the system.

Action Description CREATE_TRIP Create Trip CREATE_TRIP_WITH_APPROVAL Create Trip With Approval CREATE_TRIP_REPORT Create Trip Report APPROVE_TRIP Approve Trip OVERRIDE_WAITLIST_SETTING Override Global Waitlist Setting BYPASS_LEVEL_REQ Bypass Level Requirements for Trip EDIT_TRIPS Edit Trips EDIT_TRIP_MEDIA Edit Trip Media EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS Edit Trip Registrations DELETE_TRIPS Delete Trips DELETE_TRIP_COMMENTS Delete Trip Comments CREATE_MEETING_POINTS Create Meeting Points EDIT_MEETING_POINTS Edit Meeting Points DELETE_MEETING_POINTS Delete Meeting Points CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_SELF Create Upgrade Request For Self CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS Create Upgrade Request For Others EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ Edit Upgrade Request APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ Approve Upgrade Request DELETE_UPGRADE_REQ Delete Upgrade Request VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ View Upgrade Request (ALL levels) VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ Vote Upgrade Request CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ Comment Upgrade Request DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ Delete Comment Upgrade Request EDIT_MEMBERSHIP_PAYMENTS Edit Membership Payments CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES Create Logbook Entries SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS Sign Logbook Skills CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER Create Logbook Entries (superuser bypass) ACCESS_MARSHAL_PANEL Access Marshal Panel VIEW_CONTACT_INFO View Contact Info EDIT_UI_STRINGS Edit UI Strings

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: To ensure the stability and reliability of the AD4x4 API, we have implemented rate limiting. This means that each client is limited to a certain number of requests per minute.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The rate limiting is configured in the Nginx default.conf.template file. The current limit is set to 100 requests per minute per IP address.

docs.title: HTTP 429 Response
docs.text:
If you exceed the rate limit, the API will respond with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests status code. When you receive this response, you should:

  • Stop sending requests: Do not send any more requests until the rate limit window has reset.
  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that they have exceeded the rate limit and should try again later.
  • Implement backoff: Consider implementing an exponential backoff strategy to gradually reduce the rate of your requests.

docs.title: Swagger UI
docs.text:
Our API documentation is powered by Swagger, which provides an interactive way to explore and test the API. You can access the Swagger UI at the following URL:

https://ap.ad4x4.com/docs/swagger-ui/

docs.title: Authorizing with a Bearer Token
docs.text:
To test the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI, you'll need to obtain a bearer token and authorize your requests. Here's how to do it:

  1. Log in to the API: Send a POST request to the /api/auth/login/ endpoint with your username and password. The response will contain an access token.

  2. Authorize in Swagger:

    • Click the "Authorize" button at the top-right of the Swagger page.
    • In the dialog that appears, enter the word Bearer followed by a space and then the access token you received in the previous step. For example: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
    • Click "Authorize" to save the token.

Once you've authorized, you can make requests to any of the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing trips, including creating, viewing, registering, and managing participants.

docs.title: Trip Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Creation: A trip is created via a POST request. Depending on the creator's permissions, it may be automatically approved or require manual approval.
  2. Approval: Trips requiring approval must be approved by a user with the appropriate permissions before they become visible to regular members.
  3. Registration: Once a trip is approved, members can register for it until the cut_off time is reached or the capacity is filled.
  4. Waitlist: If a trip is full and allow_waitlist is enabled, members can join the waitlist. They will be automatically moved to the registered list if a spot becomes available.
  5. Check-in/Check-out: The trip lead or a deputy can check members in and out of the trip.

docs.title: List and Retrieve Trips
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/
    • Retrieves a list of all approved trips.
  • GET /api/trips/{id}/
    • Retrieves the full details of a single trip, including registered members and the waitlist.

docs.title: Create a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/

    • Creates a new trip. The approval_status will be set based on the user's permissions.
    • Request Body: See the CreateTripSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • lead (Member ID)
      • level (Level ID)
      • title
      • start_time
      • end_time
      • cut_off
      • capacity
      • meeting_point (MeetingPoint ID)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., start_time), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., startTime).

docs.title: Update a Trip
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/trips/{id}/
    • Updates an existing trip. Only users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission (or the trip lead) can do this.
    • Request Body: See the UpdateTripSerializer for a list of editable fields.

docs.title: Approve a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/approve/
    • Approves a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/register/
    • Registers the authenticated user for the trip.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist/
    • Adds the authenticated user to the waitlist if the trip is full.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister/
    • Cancels the authenticated user's registration for the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist).

docs.title: Participant Management
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist/
    • Manually moves a member from the waitlist to the registered list. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/removemember/
    • Removes a member from the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist). Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>, "reason": "..."}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkin/
    • Checks in one or more members to the trip.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkout/
    • Checks out one or more members from the trip.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing level upgrade requests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Members can request to be upgraded to a higher level. This process involves creating a request, which is then reviewed and voted on by authorized members (e.g., Marshals, Board Members).

docs.title: List and Retrieve Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/
    • Retrieves a list of upgrade requests. Requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single upgrade request.

docs.title: Create an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/

    • Creates a new upgrade request.
    • Request Body: See the CreateUpgradeRequestSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • applicant (Member ID of the person being nominated for upgrade)
      • target_level (Level ID)
      • applicant_reason (Text description)
      • nominated_voters (List of Member IDs)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., target_level), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., targetLevel).

docs.title: Update an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Updates an existing upgrade request. Requires EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Voting and Approval
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/vote/
    • Casts a vote on an upgrade request. Requires VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"vote": "Y"} (or "N" for No, "D" for Defer)
  • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/approve/
    • Approves an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/decline/
    • Declines an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"verdict_reason": "..."}

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/comments/
    • Retrieves all comments for a specific upgrade request.
  • POST /api/upgraderequestcomments/
    • Adds a new comment to an upgrade request. Requires CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"upgrade_request": <request_id>, "text": "..."}
  • DELETE /api/upgraderequestcomments/{id}/
    • Deletes a comment. Requires DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
